title: Why do some old maps show sea monsters?
sources: British Library Medieval Sea Monster Maps
Library of Congress Carta Marina Study

lines.text: Why did Renaissance mapmakers cover uncharted ocean waters with drawings of giant sea serpents and kraken monsters?
lines.caps: Why did ancient *maps | draw giant sea *monsters?

lines.text: It wasn't just artistic decoration or mythological fantasy.
Early ocean sailors navigated treacherous waters without modern sonar or satellite weather forecasting.
When sailors glimpsed giant squids, breaching sperm whales, or strange oarfish, terrified rumors spread.
lines.caps: Brief glimpses of giant *squids | fueled wild *legends

lines.text: Cartographers drew ferocious sea creatures to mark dangerous uncharted reefs, lethal vortex whirlpools, and shallow shoals.
They served as visual skull-and-crossbones hazard warnings for navigators sailing into the unknown.
lines.caps: A medieval *hazard sign | for uncharted deadly *waters

lines.text: The monsters on ancient maps were warnings of real oceanic perils disguised as mythical beasts.
lines.caps: Mythical beasts marking *real | and lethal oceanic *dangers!
